author: Felipe Blassioli
abstract: Rewrites a prompt, a rough idea, or a stuck investigation into a brief for the escalation-tier model on a hard, ambiguous, long-horizon problem. Unlike model-recommender (which decides placement and tier) and smart-prompt (which routes a loose intent to whatever tier fits), this skill commits to the escalation target and applies one directed transform: frame the problem and withhold the solution, strip scaffolding inherited from literal-following models, set explicit boundaries for long autonomous runs, avoid the reasoning-extraction refusal that silently falls back to a lesser model, enable subagent orchestration with each subagent's tier pinned explicitly, add a memory surface, and set the run config (effort/thinking/fallback) instead of wording effort into the prompt. When the answer is a fresh session rather than a stronger model in this one, it writes the self-contained handoff brief instead (M9) — premises labelled verified or assumed, the author's own retracted conclusions stated, and an instruction to assume another error exists. Resolves the target and every posture fact from ~/.claude/model-profiles.md at runtime (tier_to_model.escalation, delegation_aliases, and that model's profile) so it never hardcodes a model string or a per-model tip; the transform moves are the durable technique, the facts are volatile. Gates the result through prompt-audit (R2/R3/R8/R9/R10 encode the same escalation-tier checks, R12 the unpinned subagent, R13 the handoff that leans on context the fresh session lacks). Detailed moves and canonical snippet pointers live in references/fable-playbook.md (link to Anthropic's snippets, never inline them).
